text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty ALERT — policy 'prod-inference' fired for service 'inference-gateway'. Incident: HIGH 5xx spike. Triggered at 1794506789.

pagerduty: PRIMARY on-call (Alice) notified — awaiting ack. Escalation window: 60s.

Alice: acked? seeing the page now. pulling up traces and metrics.

Alice: grafana shows a sudden jump in 5xxs around 02:13 UTC, p95 latency up, request queueing on gateway. hitting autoscaler? maybe connection storm to kv-cache.

pagerduty: PRIMARY (Alice) DID NOT ACK within 60s — auto-escalating to SECONDARY (Omar).

Omar: on mobile, in meeting. @Alice can you paste the error log snippet? I can try to ack from phone.

Alice: pasting quick logs:
```
[2026-02-11T02:13:05Z] inference-gateway ERROR request_handler.cpp:427 handle_request() - 503 ServiceUnavailable - kv_cache_miss flood, backend overload
[2026-02-11T02:13:06Z] rt-sync WARN shard-3 - queue_length=1245, inflight=512
[2026-02-11T02:13:07Z] autoscaler INFO decision.cpp:97 - pending_scale_up=false, reason=rapid-surge-blocked
```

Omar: acking now from phone. ack at 1794506910. :raised_hands: will try to open the bridge if I can.

pagerduty: SECONDARY (Omar) ACK received. Escalation timer stopped.

incident-bot: created Zoom bridge: https://zoom.redwood/abc123 (link) — owner: Omar.

Jules: joining bridge. what's customer impact? any active pages from customers?

Maya: support queue shows ~18 reports in last 10m mentioning 503 and latency, mostly webhooks and batch endpoints. estimated affected customers: ~12 orgs, some high-traffic customers seeing 20-40% request failures.

Diego: quick note — we pushed model-v2.1 canary to 10% traffic 02:10 UTC. Could be related (model runtime memory pattern). Reverting canary now.

Omar: rolling back canary to v2.0 on inference-cluster-4 via canary controller. kicking rollout at 1794506955.

Alice: I'm seeing KV cache thrash in the runtime logs correlated with model change: key sizes spiked. suggestion: purge prefix cache for canary keyspace to relieve memory pressure.

Omar: running `rdwctl cache purge --prefix=canary-2026-02-11` on cluster-4.

Jules: ops note — do not restart gateway pods yet, let rollback and cache purge stabilize for 2m. restarting could exacerbate warmup.

pagerduty: SECONDARY (Omar) set responder status: investigating.

incident-bot: update: rollback completed at 1794507005. cache purge completed at 1794507012.

Maya: support logs: error rate dropping — from peak 38% -> 6% over last 3 minutes. customers still seeing intermittent failures for queued requests.

Diego: telemetry shows p95 latency falling, node memory pressure relieved. autoscaler allowed additional pods to come up but stayed within quota.

Sarah: manager escalation note — I was paged earlier due to missed secondary ack window in parallel policy. I'm on the bridge, assigning roles: Omar (incident lead), Alice (runtime), Diego (rollback verification), Jules (customer comms).

Alice: can confirm 5xxs dropped to baseline at 1794507030. will keep an eye for 10m.

Omar: moving incident to mitigation state. bridge live for 45m for monitoring.

Jules: sending a short support update to affected customers: "We've identified a canary model rollout that increased memory usage and caused cache thrashing, leading to elevated 5xx rates. We've rolled back the canary and purged affected caches — services are recovering. We'll follow up with a postmortem and timeline." (posting now)

pagerduty: INCIDENT severity downgraded to SEV-3 at 1794507040 — monitoring.

incident-bot: Reminder: if any follow-up runbook tasks needed, tag with #postmortem and assign owner.

Sarah: assigning postmortem owners: Alice (runtime analysis), Diego (deployment gating), Omar (oncall handling+runbook updates), Jules (customer comms doc).

Omar: quick action item — add a canary memory guard in deployment pipeline to prevent >X% cache growth in first 5m. filing ticket: INF-8271.

Alice: agreed. also add a PagerDuty rule tweak — stagger secondary escalation by 60s when primary is marked DND to avoid manager blips. filing PD policy note.

Jules: thanks all — will close this thread once postmortem ticket created and customers updated. :white_check_mark:
